findings.claim: The new README and MsgPack004 docs state that members of referenced-assembly types are diagnosed only by the defining assembly. This matches the recorded deliberate behavior that referenced-assembly types are not analysed by the consumer, so it is not a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed by the consumer; the defining assembly owns validation. Docs wording is consistent.

findings.claim: Diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation are now silently dropped through a ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper on every reportDiagnostic call. This also drops location-less diagnostics (Location.None) and diagnostics located in other trees. That fits L8, so it is not flagged as a defect. The wrapper is broader than the crash fix needs, which L10 says risks false negatives. The ledger does not settle whether the broad drop is intended.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] diagnostics for metadata types are intentionally absent; [L10] warns that analyzer diagnostic changes can cause wrong reports, so run the analyzer tests to confirm no existing diagnostic is dropped.

findings.claim: The README was updated with a new section, but no AnalyzerReleases entry is needed because no diagnostic is added or changed. The README section sits under the generator and analyzer area and says closed generic types from referenced assemblies are supported. That statement matches the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: The change adds no new DiagnosticDescriptor, so AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md needs no change. The README text matches REQ-2283 expected behavior.
